answer: Each agent must post a refundable stake before it can submit jobs, and a randomly chosen set of established agents checks its outputs against hidden test cases. A false identity can’t gain trust merely by multiplying accounts: each account needs its own stake, while failed checks slash that stake and lower the submitter’s future selection rate. An attacker can wander through names like cedar or anchor, but must lock up capital in every identity and risks losing it whenever those identities cheat.
